issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() as a no-argument method returning an int (see task description and UML). However, the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) — i.e. it requires a boolean parameter. This signature mismatch also affects other solution methods that call it (getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor). Students following the problem specification (no-arg method) or the UML will be confused by the solution's different API and may implement incompatible code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution conform to the specification: implement public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters that returns the total students (inscribed + guest). Update getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents() and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() to call the no-arg getTotalNumberOfStudents(). Alternatively, if the boolean parameter is intentional, update the problem statement, UML and task descriptions to specify the boolean parameter and its meaning.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) with a boolean parameter. This signature mismatch changes the expected API and creates mapping confusion for students: the exercise asks for a parameterless method that returns the total number of students, while the solution requires a boolean flag to determine whether guests are included.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the problem specification by providing a parameterless getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total number of students (inscribed + guest). If an option is needed to exclude guests, add an overloaded method (e.g. getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests)) in addition to the no-argument method so the original API from the problem/UML remains available.
